extra.message: Missing authentication on /evaluate — Anonymous attacker can reach the eval() code-injection sink without any login [verified: evaluate() at app.py:111-116 has no session/login gate before eval(expression), reachable anonymously.]

Code Injection via eval() — Arbitrary Python code execution on the server, leading to full host compromise [verified: eval(expression) at app.py:120 directly executes user-supplied form input with no sanitization or auth gate.]

Missing authentication on /lookup — Anonymous attacker can reach the OS command injection sink without any login [verified: lookup() at app.py:132-136 has no auth check before rp('nslookup '+address), reachable anonymously.]
OS Command Injection via popen — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server host [verified: popen('nslookup '+address) at app.py:140 concatenates unsanitized user input into a shell command.]

Server-Side Template Injection via render_template_string — Arbitrary code execution on the server via Jinja2 SSTI payloads (e.g. {{ config }} or RCE gadgets) [verified: app.py:189 embeds request.form['name'] directly into a template string later passed to render_template_string at line 205, classic SSTI with no escaping.]

Hardcoded Flask secret_key enabling session forgery — Attacker who knows/obtains the key can forge session cookies to set logged_in=True and bypass authentication [verified: app.secret_key is a hardcoded literal string at app.py:15 used to sign session cookies, allowing forgery if the source is known/leaked.]

Plaintext password storage and comparison — Full credential exposure if the database is compromised; no protection against credential reuse attacks [verified: login/register at app.py:48-50,62 store and compare plaintext passwords with no hashing anywhere in the file.]

Missing authentication on /xml — Anonymous attacker can reach the XXE sink without any login [verified: xml() at app.py:152-157 has no auth check; XMLParser(no_network=False, dtd_validation=True) enables XXE/SSRF, reachable anonymously.]

XXE via lxml XMLParser with entity/DTD processing enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, and potential DoS via XML external entity expansion [verified: XMLParser at app.py:157 has dtd_validation=True and no_network=False with resolve_entities not disabled, and untrusted xml is parsed via etree.fromstring, enabling XXE/SSRF/file disclosure.]

Missing authentication on /sayhi — Anonymous attacker can reach the SSTI sink without any login [verified: sayhi() at app.py:185-189 has no auth check before render_template_string on unsanitized name input.]

Plaintext password storage at registration — Database compromise or dump exposes all user passwords in cleartext [verified: register() app.py:62 stores request.form['password'] directly with no hashing, and login() app.py:50 compares plaintext, confirming plaintext storage.]

Missing authentication on /dashboard route — Unauthenticated users can access the dashboard page and its links to vulnerable functionality intended for logged-in users [verified: /dashboard at app.py:79 has no session.get('logged_in') check unlike home(), so it's reachable anonymously.]

Reflected XSS via name parameter in /sayhi — Attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JS executed in victim's browser (in addition to full SSTI takeover) [verified: name is interpolated raw via %s into HTML (app.py:189) with no escaping, then rendered through render_template_string, so unescaped HTML/JS reaches the response independent of the SSTI vector.]

Debug mode enabled in production — Werkzeug debugger console exposure can lead to remote code execution if debugger PIN is bypassed or unset [verified: app.debug = True at app.py:208 is set before app.run in the production entrypoint, enabling the Werkzeug debugger.]
